title: Zero Array Transformation IV
summary: Given an integer array nums and a 2D array queries, where each queries[i] is in the form [li, ri, vali], perform the following operations in sequence: - For each query, select a subset of indices in the range [li, ri] from nums.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a 2D array queries, where each queries[i] is in the form [li, ri, vali], perform the following operations in sequence: - For each query, select a subset of indices in the range [li, ri] from nums. - Decrement the value at each selected index by exactly vali. Determine the minimum possible non-negative value of k, such that after processing the first k queries, nums becomes a Zero Array (an array with all elements equal to zero). If it is impossible to achieve a Zero Array with any number of queries, return -1.
constraints: Each query [left,right,value] may decrement any chosen subset of covered indices by exactly value.
Process queries in order and never make an element negative.
Return the smallest prefix length that can make every nums element zero, zero if already zero, or -1 if impossible.
reference_solution:
def minimum_zero_array_query_prefix(nums,queries):
    reachable=[1]*len(nums);masks=[(1<<(target+1))-1 for target in nums]
    if all(target==0 for target in nums):return 0
    for count,(left,right,value) in enumerate(queries,1):
        for index in range(left,right+1):reachable[index]|=(reachable[index]<<value)&masks[index]
        if all((reachable[index]>>target)&1 for index,target in enumerate(nums)):return count
    return -1

hints: Each index has an independent 0/1 subset-sum problem over values from queries that cover it.
Maintain one bitset of reachable decrement totals per index and update covered bitsets once per query.
Shift by the query value, OR with prior sums, cap at nums[i], and after each query test every target bit.
Subset choices are independent across indices, so all targets being reachable is necessary and sufficient for that prefix.
